guarantees.claim: When key_init_sel is KEY_INIT_INPUT, key_init_d = key_init; when KEY_INIT_KEYMGR, key_init_d = key_sideload; otherwise (including KEY_INIT_CLEAR and default) key_init_d = prd_clearing_key_init.

assumptions.claim: key_init_sel must always be a legal one-hot encoding among KEY_INIT_INPUT, KEY_INIT_KEYMGR, KEY_INIT_CLEAR; no other values should appear.
assumptions.risk: If key_init_sel takes an illegal value, the unique case may cause synthesis to infer a priority-less select, leading to undefined or X-driven output on key_init_d, potentially corrupting key material.

assumptions.claim: prd_clearing_key_init must provide a secure clearing value (e.g., all zeros) whenever selected.
assumptions.cond: when key_init_sel is KEY_INIT_CLEAR or default
assumptions.risk: Non-zero clearing value would fail to wipe sensitive key material, potentially leaking secrets.

uncertain_points.claim: The 'unique case' construct with a default covering an illegal encoding leaves a synthesis/simulation mismatch risk: if an illegal key_init_sel value occurs, the default assignment may be ignored by synthesis, producing X or latching behavior.
uncertain_points.cond: key_init_sel is an encoding not matching any explicit branch
uncertain_points.risk: key_init_d could become X or hold previous value, disrupting key initialization and potentially exposing or corrupting key material.

uncertain_points.claim: The generation and timing of prd_clearing_key_init relative to key_init_sel transitions is not visible; it must be valid and stable when the mux selects it.
uncertain_points.cond: when key_init_sel is KEY_INIT_CLEAR or default
uncertain_points.risk: If prd_clearing_key_init is invalid or not yet asserted, key_init_d may capture a non-clearing value, violating key wipe intent.
